title: Conjecture 4.2
statement_text: For any $1\leq s\leq\frac{\sqrt{r}}{\log r}$ and $n$ large enough we have $f(n,r,s)=\frac{s^{2}(\log r)^{1-o_{r}(1)}}{r}\cdot n$.
context_text: For integers $1\le s\le r$, $f(n,r,s)$ is the maximum number of vertices one can guarantee to connect using edges of at most $s$ colours in any $r$-edge colouring of $K_n$, i.e. the largest $m$ such that every $r$-edge colouring of $K_n$ has a set $S$ of $s$ colours whose edges span a connected subgraph on at least $m$ vertices (for $s=1$ this is the Gerencsér–Gyárfás largest monochromatic component problem, $f(n,r,1)\approx n/(r-1)$). Here $o_r(1)$ is a term tending to $0$ as $r\to\infty$. Combining results of Liu, Morris and Prince with theirs, the authors show that for $n$ large compared to $r$: $f(n,r,s)=\Theta(2^s/r)\cdot n$ for $s\le(1-o_r(1))\log\log r$ (tight up to an absolute constant factor between 4 and 8 depending on divisibility properties of $r$); $f(n,r,s)=\widetilde{\Theta}_r(s^2/r)\cdot n$ for $s\le\sqrt r$ (tight up to a $\log r$ factor); $\Theta(n)$ for $s=\Theta(\sqrt r)$; $(1-e^{-\Theta(s^2/r)})n$ for $s\ge\sqrt{r\log r}$; and $n$ for $s\ge r/2$. The least precise part is the $\log r$ gap for $s\le\sqrt r$; since their lower bound for $s\approx\log\log r$ shows that a factor $(\log r)^{1-o_r(1)}$ is necessary there, they conjecture the precise form stated here throughout $s\le\sqrt r/\log r$.

title: Question 4.3
statement_text: Given $n$ and $r$, what is the smallest value of $s$ for which $f(n,r,s)=g(n,r,s)$?
context_text: For integers $1\le s\le r$, $f(n,r,s)$ is the maximum number of vertices one can guarantee to connect using edges of at most $s$ colours in any $r$-edge colouring of $K_n$, i.e. the largest $m$ such that every $r$-edge colouring of $K_n$ has a set $S$ of $s$ colours whose edges span a connected subgraph on at least $m$ vertices (for $s=1$ this is the Gerencsér–Gyárfás largest monochromatic component problem, $f(n,r,1)\approx n/(r-1)$). $g(n,r,s)$ is the minimum, over $r$-edge colourings of $K_n$, of the maximum over sets $S$ of $s$ colours of the number of vertices incident to at least one edge with colour in $S$ (for $s=1$ this is equivalent to the classical problem of covering the edges of $K_n$ by $r$ cliques, and $g(n,r,1)=\frac{1+o_r(1)}{\sqrt r}n$). Always $f(n,r,s)\le g(n,r,s)$. For $s=1$ the two functions are very different ($f\approx n/r$, $g\approx n/\sqrt r$), and the authors show they behave differently for $s\ll\sqrt r/\log r$ but similarly for $s\ge\sqrt{r\log r}$ (both are $(1-e^{-\Theta(s^2/r)})n$). Equality $f(n,r,s)=g(n,r,s)$ holds for $s\ge(r-1)/2$, and it already seems non-trivial to decide it for $s=r/2-1$ ($r$ even). For $s\ll\sqrt r$ and $n$ large there is a gap of at least about a factor $\sqrt2$, since $g(n,r,s)\ge\frac{(1+o_r(1))s}{\sqrt r}n$ while $f(n,r,s)\le\frac{(1+o_r(1))s}{\sqrt{2r}}n$.

title: Question 4.4
statement_text: Let $r\geq 2s-1\geq 3$ be integers. What is the minimum number of edges in an $r$-vertex $s$-uniform intersecting hypergraph with cover number equal to $s$?
context_text: A hypergraph is intersecting if any two of its edges share a vertex, and its cover number is the minimum size of a vertex set meeting every edge. For $r$ unrestricted this is the question of Erdős and Lovász (from their 1975 paper introducing the Local Lemma) on the minimum number of edges in an $s$-uniform intersecting hypergraph with cover number $s$, solved by Kahn in 1994, who showed the answer is linear in $s$; the new feature here is that the number of vertices is restricted to $r$. The condition $r\ge 2s-1$ is necessary (if $r\le 2s-2$, any $s-1$ vertices form a cover), and for $r=2s-1$ the answer is $\binom{2s-1}{s}$ (only the complete hypergraph works). A double counting argument shows that at least $\binom{r}{s-1}/\binom{r-s}{s-1}\ge e^{s(s-1)/(2(r-s))}$ edges are needed, so the answer grows much faster than linearly when $s\gg\sqrt{r\log r}$. The motivation is the function $g(n,r,s)$, the minimum over $r$-edge colourings of $K_n$ of the maximum number of vertices incident to an edge with colour in some set of $s$ colours; the authors essentially solve a weakening in which the uniformity may be somewhat larger than the cover number bound, and a good answer would give more precise bounds on $g(n,r,s)$.

title: Question 4.5
statement_text: What is the minimum number of edges in an $r$-vertex intersecting hypergraph if any subset of $m$ vertices needs to contain at least $t$ edges?
context_text: A hypergraph is intersecting if any two of its edges share a vertex, and its cover number is the minimum size of a vertex set meeting every edge. An edge is contained in a vertex subset if it is a subset of it. $g(n,r,s)$ is the minimum, over $r$-edge colourings of $K_n$, of the maximum over sets $S$ of $s$ colours of the number of vertices incident to at least one edge with colour in $S$ (for $s=1$ this is equivalent to the classical problem of covering the edges of $K_n$ by $r$ cliques, and $g(n,r,1)=\frac{1+o_r(1)}{\sqrt r}n$). Always $f(n,r,s)\le g(n,r,s)$. The authors show that determining $g(n,r,s)$ is equivalent to an extremal problem on intersecting (multi-)hypergraphs on the $r$ colours: from a colouring, each vertex $v$ of $K_n$ gives the edge consisting of the colours at $v$, which is intersecting, and conversely an $r$-vertex intersecting hypergraph $H$ in which every set of $r-s$ vertices contains at least $t$ edges yields $g(n,r,s)\le n-t\lfloor n/|E(H)|\rfloor$; only edges of size at least $s+1$ are useful, and they mostly use $(s+1)$-uniform $H$. Hence, if multi-hypergraphs are allowed, the question (for $m=r-s$) is essentially equivalent to determining $g(n,r,s)$, and most of the authors' results on $g$ come from results on this question.

title: Question 4.6
statement_text: For which values of $r,s$ does there exist an $r$-vertex, $(s+1)$-uniform intersecting hypergraph in which all sets of size $r-s$ contain the same positive number of edges?
context_text: A hypergraph is intersecting if any two of its edges share a vertex, and its cover number is the minimum size of a vertex set meeting every edge. $g(n,r,s)$ is the minimum, over $r$-edge colourings of $K_n$, of the maximum over sets $S$ of $s$ colours of the number of vertices incident to at least one edge with colour in $S$ (for $s=1$ this is equivalent to the classical problem of covering the edges of $K_n$ by $r$ cliques, and $g(n,r,1)=\frac{1+o_r(1)}{\sqrt r}n$). Always $f(n,r,s)\le g(n,r,s)$. The authors show that determining $g(n,r,s)$ is equivalent to an extremal problem on intersecting (multi-)hypergraphs on the $r$ colours: from a colouring, each vertex $v$ of $K_n$ gives the edge consisting of the colours at $v$, which is intersecting, and conversely an $r$-vertex intersecting hypergraph $H$ in which every set of $r-s$ vertices contains at least $t$ edges yields $g(n,r,s)\le n-t\lfloor n/|E(H)|\rfloor$; only edges of size at least $s+1$ are useful, and they mostly use $(s+1)$-uniform $H$. If an $(s+1)$-uniform intersecting $H$ has every set of $r-s$ vertices containing the same number of edges, this gives $g(n,r,s)\le\left(1-\binom{r-s-1}{s}/\binom{r}{s}\right)n$, which is tight under some divisibility conditions; the authors use the complete $(s+1)$-uniform hypergraph to obtain their precise result at the end of the range. The question has a design-like flavour, asking for a somewhat pseudorandom intersecting hypergraph; approximate versions give approximate results on $g(n,r,s)$.
